native_text: An obliging person, seeking contacts with other people. New faces in one's environment. General Remarks The observation and research of illness requires a great deal of care and tact. The author has been particularly careful in all of his statements. No-one should be tempted to give a diagnosis on the basis of the cosmic picture alone because it is impossible. So many factors add to the situation which is shown in the chart, but which can only be released under special circumstances. These cannot be foreseen from the chart. One should always consider that Biological Correspondences are based on cooperation with doctors. The Biological Correspondences can become effective through various circumstances. One must always be very careful in interpreting disease. Those who work on cosmobiology must be constantly aware that it is nonsense to read the destiny from the stars alone. It is also important to have some knowledge of psychology and medicine and a rich experience of life if one wants to help not only one's own family but others too. With every word spoken by the cosmoblological investigator one should be conscious of the responsibility and the damaging consequences which the wrong words could have. One does not help others by making them afraid of the future but must use every opportunity to build up their self-confidence and their self-consciousness of their own value. Those who advise others should always remember that it is not for them to bring about a decision in the life of another. It is for the cosmobiologist to give help and build up confidence in others so that they can make their own decisions to the best of their ability. Translator's Notes Since the appearance of the first English edition in 1960, The Combination of Stellar Influences has universally established itself as a standard work of outstanding importance. In preparing this translation of the 1961 supplement we have followed Dr. Roosedale's translation of technical terms wherever appropriate, e.g., "Gestim" has been translated as "stellar body" to refer equally to planet, Sun or Moon. Likewise, quotations from the main body of the text have always been given as they appear in the original translation. As many readers may be as yet unfamiliar with the 90o-circle method of charting described in this supplement, it should be mentioned that this method is usually employed in conjunction with a 90o-dial. This is a simple instrument which enables one to examine all the mid-point axes in a chart in a few minutes. It is an absolutely essential tool for work in this field. Meanwhile it is hoped that this supplementary material will further stimulate research along the lines pioneered by Mr, Ebertin. Charles Harvey Use Hodges May 1969 It has always been the intention that the individual statements given in The Combination of Stellar Influences should only be used as suggestions for the interpretation of the combinations and never as though they were immutable and finally established rules. The correspondences of each cosmic factor should be arranged together into a total picture and the meaning of the individual components combined into a coordinated whole. Users repeatedly confirm the often quite disconcerting agreement between some of the interpretations as given and the characteristics and events of an individual's life. But in this very fact there is a danger. A statement must be confirmed not just once but many times and repeatedly if it is to be brought to a level of certainty upon which one can base defensible diagnosis or prognosis. Moreover, one should not neglect to take into account the present conditions of the individual, his or her stage of development, age, environment, walk of life and other factors, and to combine all of these considerations with the findings from the birth chart. The cosmic factor alone is never sufficient, nor ever can be. Since the 1950 edition numerous advances have been made in cosmobiology which increasingly accentuate the difference between it and the type of "soothsaying" that is so often practiced in the name of astrology. Many particulars have been thoroughly worked out, conclusive statements evolved and work made easier and rationalized with suitable modem methods. The advantages of the 90-degree-circle have been increasingly recognized so that now no skilled practitioners would consider themselves capable of making a reliable diagnosis or prognosis without it. After World War II, Reinhold Ebertin developed a new method of charting (K2) which combines the 90° and the usual 360° systems on one comprehensive chart form. We may note here in connection with illustrations E/l and E/2, that the 90° circle is placed round the outside of the usual 360° zodiac. The first 30° contain the cardinal signs: Taurus, Leo, Scorpio, Aquarius; 60o-90o the mutable signs: Gemini, Virgo, Sagittarius, Pisces. This means that when the positions are marked on the 90° circle, conjunction, square and opposition aspects all fall together and the semisquare and sesquiquadrate aspects fall opposite. Thus when several positions fall together one can see at once which factors are in relationship to each other. For example, here in E/2, Jupiter, Neptune, Ascendant and Mars form such a complex. The full advantages of this system only become really apparent when one is working with transits and directions. In this connection attention is drawn to Angewandte Kosmobiologie {Applied Cosmobiology). A further help is Gesicherte Schnelldiagnose {Certain, Quick Diagnosis), which shows the way in which the combinations in a chart will work out. The cosmic state of a stellar body is determined from a synthesis of its various aspects and mid-point-combinations. It can be very quickly determined with the aid of the 90o-circle. Example E/2 is the chart of the Italian racing cyclist Fausto Coppi. In example E/3, only the cosmic state of Mars has been drawn in. Mars lies in the mid-points Moon/MC and Sun/Pluto. (In precise work with mid-points an orb of only 1V20 should be allowed.) It should also be remembered that one speaks of "indirect mid-points" when a factor is not actually on the mid-point axis itself but at a 45° angle to this axis. In this case Mars is almost exactly at the mid-point, or axis, of Sun/Pluto and 45° from the Moon/MC axis. • Mars = Moon/MC: "The devotion to a task or cause both in body and soul... industriousness, the urge to strive constantly for the fulfillment of an objective. .. ." • Mars = Sun/Pluto: "The desire to perform record achievements ... over exertion or overtaxing ones powers.. .. The tendency to work until physical breakdown occurs." These statements certainly correspond with the character of a racing cyclist. The cosmic states such as in example E/3 and in the examples that follow are delineated as part of a "structural-picture" or as "structural-elements." Structural-element is a term synonymous with cosmic state. The structural picture is the "picture" in which all the structural-elements of the chart are contained. The great value of the structural-elements lies in the fact that they are open to comparison in different charts, as will be shown in detail later. However one can only compare charts adequately when they have been erected by a fixed system. As the Sun is at its highest position in Cancer, 0° Cancer is placed at the top of the chart and this marks the zero point of the 90°-circle, as is shown in E/2 and E/3. When drawing up the structural-picture we further simplify things. The factor under examination (Mars in this case) is set down, a vertical line is drawn under it, and the individual mid-points grouped round it as is shown in E/4. Groupings of other factors are seen round E/3. The strict order of some of the positions has been changed around but it in fact seems to be unimportant whether Mars is in the middle of Moon/MC or MC/Moon. Experience has shown that for the most part the important thing is which factors are combined, while it often seems to be of less importance how these factors are actually grouped. Examples of this are given later. To illustrate this further the structural-elements (cosmic-states) of Jupiter, Pluto and Moon, examples E/5-E/7, have been added. By comparing the structural-elements of different charts it is possible to replace earlier dogmatic, artificial and inspired "interpretations" with reliable, scientifically established statements. The cosmo-psychogram was developed jointly by Reinhold and Dr. Baldur Ebertin. Its basis is explained in detail and substantiated with numerous illustrations in Die kosmischen Grundlagen unseres Lebens. Its use pre-dates the introduction of structural-elements in chart analysis and in setting up the cosmo-psychogram somewhat larger orbs are used for aspects. Examples E/8 and E/9 show two quite dissimilar cosmo-psychograms. The cosmo-psychogram shows in the form of a seventeen rayed diagram the results obtained by evaluating the structural-elements of a chart according to a fixed key. The bottom four rays show the individual's "type-composition," i.e., the proportion of tension and relaxation, and of inward and outward interest (the tendency to introversion or extroversion). The type-composition is based upon the sign positions of the individual horoscopic factors. The middle circle of the cosmo-psychogram shows the distance-value of each heavenly body. This is based upon its distance from the Earth, from value 0 for apogee to 100 at perigee. Each of the 13 birth chart factors is represented by a ray on the cosmo-psychogram. The white inner portion of each ray is its positive value and the black outer portion its negative value. The length of the ray is determined by evaluating the factors mid-points and aspects according to a fixed key. The total white section is defined as the positive "kernel" and the total black section as the negative "mantle." If we compare the two cases E/8 and E/9, it is immediately apparent that in E/8 there is a very large positive kernel and a weak negative mantle, while in E/9 on the other hand there is a smaller positive kernel and a very much larger negative mantle. Furthermore, while E/8 gives an unbroken and coherent impression E/9 appears ragged and disjointed. General Remarks The observation and research of illness requires a great deal of care and tact. The author has been particularly careful in all of his statements. No-one should be tempted to give a diagnosis on the basis of the cosmic picture alone because it is impossible. So many factors add to the situation which is shown in the chart, but which can only be released under special circumstances. These cannot be foreseen from the chart. One should always consider that Biological Correspondences are based on cooperation with doctors. The Biological Correspondences can become effective through various circumstances. One must always be very careful in interpreting disease. Those who work on cosmobiology must be constantly aware that it is nonsense to read the destiny from the stars alone. It is also important to have some knowledge of psychology and medicine and a rich experience of life if one wants to help not only one's own family but others too. With every word spoken by the cosmoblological investigator one should be conscious of the responsibility and the damaging consequences which the wrong words could have. One does not help others by making them afraid of the future but must use every opportunity to build up their self-confidence and their self-consciousness of their own value. Those who advise others should always remember that it is not for them to bring about a decision in the life of another. It is for the cosmobiologist to give help and build up confidence in others so that they can make their own decisions to the best of their ability. Translator's Notes Since the appearance of the first English edition in 1960, The Combination of Stellar Influences has universally established itself as a standard work of outstanding importance. In preparing this translation of the 1961 supplement we have followed Dr. Roosedale's translation of technical terms wherever appropriate, e.g., "Gestim" has been translated as "stellar body" to refer equally to planet, Sun or Moon. Likewise, quotations from the main body of the text have always been given as they appear in the original translation. As many readers may be as yet unfamiliar with the 90o-circle method of charting described in this supplement, it should be mentioned that this method is usually employed in conjunction with a 90o-dial. This is a simple instrument which enables one to examine all the mid-point axes in a chart in a few minutes. It is an absolutely essential tool for work in this field. Meanwhile it is hoped that this supplementary material will further stimulate research along the lines pioneered by Mr, Ebertin. Charles Harvey Use Hodges May 1969 It has always been the intention that the individual statements given in The Combination of Stellar Influences should only be used as suggestions for the interpretation of the combinations and never as though they were immutable and finally established rules. The correspondences of each cosmic factor should be arranged together into a total picture and the meaning of the individual components combined into a coordinated whole. Users repeatedly confirm the often quite disconcerting agreement between some of the interpretations as given and the characteristics and events of an individual's life. But in this very fact there is a danger. A statement must be confirmed not just once but many times and repeatedly if it is to be brought to a level of certainty upon which one can base defensible diagnosis or prognosis. Moreover, one should not neglect to take into account the present conditions of the individual, his or her stage of development, age, environment, walk of life and other factors, and to combine all of these considerations with the findings from the birth chart. The cosmic factor alone is never sufficient, nor ever can be. Since the 1950 edition numerous advances have been made in cosmobiology which increasingly accentuate the difference between it and the type of "soothsaying" that is so often practiced in the name of astrology. Many particulars have been thoroughly worked out, conclusive statements evolved and work made easier and rationalized with suitable modem methods. The advantages of the 90-degree-circle have been increasingly recognized so that now no skilled practitioners would consider themselves capable of making a reliable diagnosis or prognosis without it. After World War II, Reinhold Ebertin developed a new method of charting (K2) which combines the 90° and the usual 360° systems on one comprehensive chart form. We may note here in connection with illustrations E/l and E/2, that the 90° circle is placed round the outside of the usual 360° zodiac. The first 30° contain the cardinal signs: Taurus, Leo, Scorpio, Aquarius; 60o-90o the mutable signs: Gemini, Virgo, Sagittarius, Pisces. This means that when the positions are marked on the 90° circle, conjunction, square and opposition aspects all fall together and the semisquare and sesquiquadrate aspects fall opposite. Thus when several positions fall together one can see at once which factors are in relationship to each other. For example, here in E/2, Jupiter, Neptune, Ascendant and Mars form such a complex. The full advantages of this system only become really apparent when one is working with transits and directions. In this connection attention is drawn to Angewandte Kosmobiologie {Applied Cosmobiology). A further help is Gesicherte Schnelldiagnose {Certain, Quick Diagnosis), which shows the way in which the combinations in a chart will work out. The cosmic state of a stellar body is determined from a synthesis of its various aspects and mid-point-combinations. It can be very quickly determined with the aid of the 90o-circle. Example E/2 is the chart of the Italian racing cyclist Fausto Coppi. In example E/3, only the cosmic state of Mars has been drawn in. Mars lies in the mid-points Moon/MC and Sun/Pluto. (In precise work with mid-points an orb of only 1V20 should be allowed.) It should also be remembered that one speaks of "indirect mid-points" when a factor is not actually on the mid-point axis itself but at a 45° angle to this axis. In this case Mars is almost exactly at the mid-point, or axis, of Sun/Pluto and 45° from the Moon/MC axis. • Mars = Moon/MC: "The devotion to a task or cause both in body and soul... industriousness, the urge to strive constantly for the fulfillment of an objective. .. ." • Mars = Sun/Pluto: "The desire to perform record achievements ... over exertion or overtaxing ones powers.. .. The tendency to work until physical breakdown occurs." These statements certainly correspond with the character of a racing cyclist. The cosmic states such as in example E/3 and in the examples that follow are delineated as part of a "structural-picture" or as "structural-elements." Structural-element is a term synonymous with cosmic state. The structural picture is the "picture" in which all the structural-elements of the chart are contained. By comparing the structural-elements of different charts it is possible to replace earlier dogmatic, artificial and inspired "interpretations" with reliable, scientifically established statements. The cosmo-psychogram was developed jointly by Reinhold and Dr. Baldur Ebertin. Its basis is explained in detail and substantiated with numerous illustrations in Die kosmischen Grundlagen unseres Lebens. Its use pre-dates the introduction of structural-elements in chart analysis and in setting up the cosmo-psychogram somewhat larger orbs are used for aspects. Examples E/8 and E/9 show two quite dissimilar cosmo-psychograms. The cosmo-psychogram shows in the form of a seventeen rayed diagram the results obtained by evaluating the structural-elements of a chart according to a fixed key. The bottom four rays show the individual's "type-composition," i.e., the proportion of tension and relaxation, and of inward and outward interest (the tendency to introversion or extroversion). The type-composition is based upon the sign positions of the individual horoscopic factors. The middle circle of the cosmo-psychogram shows the distance-value of each heavenly body. This is based upon its distance from the Earth, from value 0 for apogee to 100 at perigee. Each of the 13 birth chart factors is represented by a ray on the cosmo-psychogram. The white inner portion of each ray is its positive value and the black outer portion its negative value.
